articles.title: From Michelin Stars to Grocery Aisles: Gymkhana Brings Premium Indian Sauces to America
articles.excerpt: The two-Michelin-starred London restaurant's CPG line launches in Whole Foods nationwide, backed by an $8.5 million Series A as Indian cuisine enters its premium moment in the US.
articles.image_caption: A rich assortment of Indian spices and curry ingredients
articles.nri_angle: A Michelin-starred Indian brand entering American grocery shelves signals that Indian cuisine has arrived at the premium tier, validating what diaspora families have always known about their food.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Chipotle of Indian Food Is No Longer a Punchline
articles.excerpt: From Rasa's East Coast expansion to new openings in Columbus and Gastonia, Indian fast-casual dining is finally hitting its stride across America.
articles.image_caption: A vibrant Indian curry bowl with rice and fresh accompaniments
articles.nri_angle: The Indian fast-casual boom validates diaspora food culture while raising questions about how much simplification is needed to make Indian cuisine mainstream in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Mother's Haldi Doodh Is Now a $7 Turmeric Latte
articles.excerpt: As turmeric mentions surge 157 percent on American menus, NRIs are watching their grandmothers' remedies get repackaged — and repriced — as premium wellness trends.
articles.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root, the ancient Indian spice now trending as a wellness superfood
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are watching their grandmothers' kitchen remedies get rebranded as premium Western wellness trends — a bittersweet validation that raises questions about cultural ownership and pricing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Naan Next Door: Indian Food Finally Cracks America's Fast-Casual Code
articles.excerpt: From Austin to D.C., a new generation of Indian fast-casual chains is proving that tikka masala can sit alongside Chipotle — and investors are betting billions it will.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of chicken tikka masala, the most popular dish at Indian fast-casual chains across America
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans finally see their cuisine in the fast-casual mainstream — elevated alongside Chipotle and Cava as a legitimate national dining format.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The British-Indian Invasion: Michelin-Starred Gymkhana and Cult-Favourite Dishoom Set Sights on America
articles.excerpt: London's two most celebrated Indian dining brands are crossing the Atlantic simultaneously — one with simmer sauces in every Whole Foods, the other with a Manhattan debut backed by LVMH.
articles.image_caption: Dishoom's signature retro Bombay aesthetic at one of its UK locations
articles.nri_angle: Two iconic London Indian brands entering the US simultaneously signals Indian cuisine has arrived as a global luxury export, not a niche immigrant offering.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Toddy Shops to Tribeca: How Kerala Became America's Most Wanted Regional Cuisine
articles.excerpt: With three new Manhattan restaurants, a Michelin star in San Francisco, and a Datassential nod as the 'Cuisine to Know for 2026,' Kerala's coconut-laced cooking has arrived on the global stage.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Kerala sadya feast served on a banana leaf with an array of vegetarian dishes
articles.nri_angle: For the estimated 500,000 Malayalis in the US, Kerala's prominence in American fine dining validates a cuisine long invisible in the mainstream.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Liquid Gold Rush: How Ghee Became a $62 Billion Global Phenomenon — and Why Your Nani Saw It Coming
articles.excerpt: North America is now the fastest-growing ghee market in the world, driven by keto diets, Ayurvedic wellness trends, and a diaspora that never stopped cooking with it.
articles.image_caption: A jar of golden homemade ghee, the traditional Indian clarified butter
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up watching their grandmothers simmer butter into liquid gold, the West's sudden obsession with ghee is both vindicating and a little amusing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Darjeeling to 2,000 Walmarts: Indian Tea Gets Its Zero-Tariff American Moment
articles.excerpt: A new US-India trade deal eliminates duties on Indian tea, giving exporters a competitive edge over China just as brands like Vahdam are scaling up coast to coast.
articles.image_caption: A Darjeeling tea garden in the misty hills of West Bengal, India — source of the world's most prized tea leaves
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who have long wished they could get real Indian tea at the corner store instead of settling for generic blends, the surge of Indian tea brands into mainstream US retail hits close to home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Kulfi Effect: How Indian Ice Cream Is Winning Over America, One Saffron Scoop at a Time
articles.excerpt: From Malai's masala chai scoops in Manhattan to Kesar Creamery's gulab jamun gelato in Texas, Indian-inspired ice cream brands are reshaping the American frozen dessert landscape — and making NRIs feel right at home.
articles.image_caption: Traditional malai kulfi garnished with pistachios, served on a plate
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American entrepreneurs are bringing the tastes of home — kulfi, falooda, saffron pistachio — to mainstream American ice cream shops, giving NRIs nostalgic flavours and normalising Indian desserts for a wider audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Baked Oats Chaat to Rasmalai Tres Leches: India's Viral Fusion Recipes Are Rewriting the Global Cookbook
articles.excerpt: A new generation of Indian food creators is mashing up dosa with gochujang, rasmalai with tres leches, and ragi with chocolate lava cake — and racking up tens of millions of views in the process.
articles.image_caption: A colourful plate of papri chaat topped with chutneys, yogurt, and crispy sev
articles.nri_angle: NRI home cooks are recreating India's viral fusion recipes with ingredients from Patel Brothers and Amazon, adapting them to American kitchens and contributing to a global feedback loop that is making Indian food culture more dynamic than ever.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From a Family Clay Oven to a James Beard Nod: The Immigrant Story Behind Las Vegas's Hottest Indian Restaurant
articles.excerpt: Tamba — named for the Hindi word for copper — earned a Best New Restaurant finalist nod from the James Beard Foundation in its first year, capping a three-decade journey that began with an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant.
articles.image_caption: A traditional tandoor clay oven, the centrepiece of Indian cooking that gave the Dhillon family's first restaurant its name
articles.nri_angle: Tamba's journey from an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant to a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist mirrors the larger arc of Indian cuisine's ascent in America, offering diaspora families a powerful narrative of generational ambition rewarded.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
